modelStereotypes.name: GraphRagEntity
modelStereotypes.description: Graph-RAG settings of a class: match strategy, relevance anchor, extraction hints and group.

stereotypeProperties.name: graphRagMatch
stereotypeProperties.description: exact | fuzzy: how an extracted instance is matched to existing entities

stereotypeProperties.name: graphRagFuzzyThreshold
stereotypeProperties.description: Score (0-1) at or above which a fuzzy match merges automatically; empty = 0.92

stereotypeProperties.name: graphRagReviewBand
stereotypeProperties.description: Score (0-1) at or above which, below the threshold, a pair goes to review; empty = 0.75

stereotypeProperties.name: graphRagAnchor
stereotypeProperties.description: auto | true | false: whether the relevance gate uses this class; auto = when identified

stereotypeProperties.name: graphRagExtractionHints
stereotypeProperties.description: Free text appended to the extraction prompt: labels, formats, where values appear

stereotypeProperties.name: graphRagGroup
stereotypeProperties.description: Extraction group; empty = the class's domain

modelStereotypes.name: GraphRagIdentity
modelStereotypes.description: The attribute is part of the class's identity key.

stereotypeProperties.name: graphRagIdentityOrder
stereotypeProperties.description: Position in a composite identity key (1-based); empty = declaration order

stereotypeProperties.name: graphRagNormalise
stereotypeProperties.description: trim | casefold | digits | date | amount | none; empty = the default of the type

modelStereotypes.name: GraphRagEmbed
modelStereotypes.description: The String attribute is indexed on its own in the vector store.

classes.name: Organisation
classes.description: An organisation named in an architecture document: the agency, department or IT directorate that issues or owns systems (PBGC, GPO, FDOT District 5, VITA, DSI du CHSE), a vendor or integrator (Kapsch, SwRI, Gainwell, DXC, Net-Assembly), a hosting provider (Digital Ocean) or a consortium.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Name as printed, in full (U.S. Government Publishing Office, Centre Hospitalier Sud Essonne)

attributes.name: acronym
attributes.description: Acronym printed next to the name or used alone in the text (GPO, FDOT, DIT-T, VITA, CHSE, OIMT)

attributes.name: country
attributes.description: Country or state/region when stated (Vermont, North Carolina, France)

relations.name: kind
relations.description: Role the organisation plays in the documents

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: Organisations appear on the cover page ('Prepared by', 'Published by', 'Edition :', 'Prepared for'), in the document control table ('Created By', 'Reviewed By', 'Approved By' followed by a name and an organisation), in copyright lines and in the text as the owner, operator, vendor or maintainer of a system ('maintained by DIT-T', 'hébergé chez Digital Ocean'). Use the full name as name and put the acronym in acronym; when only an acronym is printed, use it as the name.

classes.name: Person
classes.description: A named person: author, reviewer, approver or point of contact of an architecture document, or a role holder named in the text (Chief Information Officer, Chief Enterprise Architect, project manager).

attributes.name: fullName
attributes.description: First name and last name as printed (Clay Weston, Vadim Chepegin, Abhi Jay Krishnan)

attributes.name: role
attributes.description: Role or title as printed (Project Manager, MBDSS Program Manager, State Auditor, Faculty Coach, Chef de projet)

attributes.name: email
attributes.description: E-mail address when printed

relations.name: organisation
relations.description: The organisation the person belongs to, when printed next to the name ('Clay Weston, SwRI', 'Tushar Patel, FDOT')

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: People are printed on the cover ('Prepared by:', 'Edited by:', 'Contributors:', 'Team Members:', 'Rédigé par'), in the document control or approval table (Created By / Reviewed By / Approved By, 'Printed Name', 'Signature') and in revision histories ('Author', 'Primary Author(s)'). Do not extract fictional characters of worked examples.

classes.name: BusinessArea
classes.description: A top-level business domain or line of business that groups business capabilities and processes: MITA business areas (Business Relationship Management, Care Management, Eligibility & Enrollment Management, Financial Management), a state's lines of business, a hospital's 'pôles', an agency's mission areas.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Name of the business area as printed (Eligibility & Enrollment Management, Driver Services, Gestion administrative du patient)

attributes.name: code
attributes.description: Short code printed before the name when the framework uses one (MITA: BR, CM, CO, EE, FM, MM, OM, PE, PL, PM)

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Overview paragraph of the business area

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: Business areas are section headings of the form '3.5 EE -- Eligibility & Enrollment Management' in MITA self-assessments, rows of a business capability matrix, or 'lines of business' / 'domaines métier' lists in EA blueprints and master plans (schéma directeur).

classes.name: BusinessCapability
classes.description: A business capability or business process that the organisation performs and that systems support: a MITA business process (EE01 Determine Member Eligibility, CM02 Manage Case Information), a DMV service (issue driver licence credentials, vehicle titling and registration), a hospital function (dossier patient informatisé, facturation), an EA blueprint business function.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Name of the capability or process as printed (Determine Member Eligibility, Manage Provider Recoupment, Records and monitors license plates and vehicle ownership)

attributes.name: code
attributes.description: Process code printed before the name when the framework uses one (EE01, CM07, FM15)

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Description of what the capability covers, including findings and gap analysis text

attributes.name: currentMaturity
attributes.description: Current (As-Is) maturity level when a maturity scale is printed (MITA 'As Is MML 1' to 5)

attributes.name: targetMaturity
attributes.description: Target (To-Be) maturity level when printed (MITA 'To Be MML')

relations.name: businessArea
relations.description: The business area the capability belongs to (the section or matrix row group it is printed under)

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: Capabilities are printed as numbered sub-headings 'EE01 -- Determine Member Eligibility' with 'As Is' / 'To Be' maturity levels, as rows of a 'Business Capability Matrix', as the service described next to each legacy system ('SADLS: Issues Driver License Credentials'), or as 'processus métier' / 'fonctions' in French documents. Extract one entity per process, not per paragraph.

classes.name: Technology
classes.description: A technology product, platform, protocol or standard named in the documents: an operating system (Windows Server, Solaris, Ubuntu 22.04), a database (Oracle, MySQL 8, MongoDB, SQL Server), middleware (WebSphere, ESB, Elasticsearch), network or security equipment (Cisco Nexus, Palo Alto, Aruba), storage (Swift, S3, Nimble), an end-user device (Dell Optiplex), a language or framework (PHP, J2EE, .NET) or a standard or protocol (OAIS, HIPAA 5010, X12 834, SFTP, TLS, REST).

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Product, protocol or standard name as printed, without the version (Microsoft SQL Server, VMware vSphere, Palo Alto, MongoDB, SFTP)

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Version or release when printed (22.04, 8, 2019, 5010, v3)

relations.name: vendor
relations.description: The vendor or standards body when named (Microsoft, Cisco, The Open Group, W3C)

relations.name: category
relations.description: Category of technology

relations.name: status
relations.description: Lifecycle status in the organisation's standards when printed (standard, emerging, retiring)

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: Technologies appear in standards catalogs as 'Component / Standard / Version' columns, in 'Third Party Components', 'COTS', 'Composants logiciels utilisés', 'Biblothèques structurantes' and 'Requis' lists, in infrastructure descriptions ('serveurs Linux (Ubuntu 22.04)', 'Base de données : MySQL 8') and in text ('Oracle SQL database', 'Shibboleth for authentication'). One entity per product, with the version in version, not in the name. Vendors go to the Organisation class and are linked through vendor.

classes.name: Site
classes.description: A physical or cloud location where systems run: a data center, a server room ('salle serveurs'), a hospital or agency site, a cloud region or a hosting provider's data centers ('data centers européens', 'Data Center US Geographical Based').

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Name of the site as printed (site de Dourdan, site d'Etampes, GPO Data Center, Azure UK South)

attributes.name: location
attributes.description: City, region or country when printed (Raleigh NC, Europe)

relations.name: kind
relations.description: Kind of site

relations.name: operator
relations.description: The organisation that operates the site when named (Digital Ocean, the state IT department)

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: Sites are named in infrastructure sections and network diagrams: 'deux salles serveurs', 'sur chacun des deux sites', 'hébergé chez Digital Ocean, en data centers européens', 'Data Center', 'Location'. Extract one entity per distinct site; when a document only says 'two sites' without names, extract nothing.

classes.name: NetworkZone
classes.description: A network zone or security tier that separates components: DMZ, application zone, data zone, administration zone, 'zone d'accès', 'zone de stockage', VITAM 'découpage en zones', an internal network or a VPN tunnel to a partner.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Name of the zone as printed (DMZ, zone applicative, zone données, Science DMZ, Internal Network)

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: What the zone hosts and the filtering rules applied to it

relations.name: site
relations.description: The site the zone belongs to, when the document ties zones to a site

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: Zones appear in 'Découpage en zones', 'network zoning', 'Network Diagram' and security sections, and as the zones a flow crosses ('zones réseau traversées par les flux'). One entity per named zone.

classes.name: InfrastructureNode
classes.description: A piece of infrastructure that hosts or connects components: a physical or virtual server, a mainframe, a cluster node, a network device (core switch, firewall, wireless access point), a storage array, an appliance (UPS, backup appliance), a cloud instance or an end-user device model. Named by its hostname, role or model as printed.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Hostname, role name or model as printed (serveur de réplication, coeur de réseau, DMV mainframe, HPE ProLiant, Cisco Nexus core switch)

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.description: Number of identical nodes when printed ('3 x', 'double coeur de réseau' = 2)

attributes.name: cpuCount
attributes.description: Number of CPUs or vCPUs when printed

attributes.name: memoryGb
attributes.description: RAM in gigabytes when printed (Go, GB)

attributes.name: storageGb
attributes.description: Local or attached storage in gigabytes when printed (convert To/TB to GB)

attributes.name: bandwidth
attributes.description: Link bandwidth for network nodes and links as printed (350 Mbit, 10 Gbps)

relations.name: kind
relations.description: Kind of node

relations.name: environment
relations.description: Environment the node belongs to when printed (production, test, PRA)

relations.name: technology
relations.description: The main product or operating system running on the node (Windows Server, VMware vSphere, Ubuntu 22.04)

relations.name: zone
relations.description: The network zone the node sits in, when stated

relations.name: site
relations.description: The site or data center hosting the node, when stated

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: Nodes appear in 'Infrastructure technique', 'Physical Architecture', 'Deployment Diagram', 'Network Diagram', sizing tables ('dimensionnement': CPU / RAM / disque per server) and standards catalogs ('Server Hardware: HPE Proliant', 'Core/Peripheral Switch: Cisco Nexus'). Use the role or hostname as name; the product goes to technology. Do not create a node for a product that is only listed as a standard without an instance.

classes.name: DataObject
classes.description: A business data object that systems store or exchange: member eligibility, provider record, claim, crash report, vehicle registration, driver licence, commande (order), dossier patient, archival information package (SIP/AIP/DIP), metadata. Named at the level documents use, not at the field level.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Name of the data object as printed (Provider Network Data, Medicare beneficiary eligibility, Placement, Commande, Archival Information Package)

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: What the data object contains, as described in data model or file description sections

attributes.name: sensitivity
attributes.description: Confidentiality or regulatory classification when printed (PHI, PII, HIPAA, données de santé, secret)

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: Data objects are named in 'Logical Data Model', 'Information Packages', 'User View of Data', 'Data Exchanges' tables, 'Structure d'une commande' and 'données' sections, and as the subject of each interface file (Placement, Payment and Adjustments, Demographic). Extract the object, not its individual fields (fields belong to DataElement under the exchange).

classes.name: QualityRequirement
classes.description: A quality attribute requirement or non-functional constraint stated for a system: availability target, performance limit, security rule, maintainability or usability scenario, real-time constraint, failover. Value object owned by its system.

attributes.name: statement
attributes.description: The requirement or scenario as written ('The system shall support up to 10k data for both Inbound and Outbound files', 'haute disponibilité du système sur deux salles serveurs')

attributes.name: metric
attributes.description: Quantified target when printed (99.9 %, < 2 s, 350 Mbit, RPO 1 h)

relations.name: attribute
relations.description: The quality attribute the requirement addresses

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: Found under 'Quality Attributes', 'Non-Functional Requirements', 'Architectural Constraints', 'Design Assumptions and Constraints', 'Behavior and Performance', 'Safety, Security, and Privacy', 'Contraintes et objectifs', 'PCA/PRA'. One value object per stated requirement, attached to the system the section is about.

classes.name: ArchitectureDecision
classes.description: A design decision or general orientation recorded for a system, with its rationale: choice of a pattern (MVP, SOA, layered), of a hosting model, of open source, of REST APIs, of a storage offer. Value object owned by its system.

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Short title of the decision ('Why MVP pattern?', 'Open Source', 'API REST', 'Architecture multi-tenants')

attributes.name: rationale
attributes.description: The justification given in the document, in its own words

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: Found under 'Orientations générales', 'Design Considerations', 'Solution Strategy', 'Patterns and Tactics', 'Rationale', 'Design Rationale', 'Justification des choix techniques'. One value object per decision; keep the rationale text as printed.

classes.name: Component
classes.description: A subsystem, module, service, database, data store, user interface, batch job or API that is part of a system, as described in its architecture document (Content Management Subsystem, Archival Subsystem, Session Authentication (SA-BS), Business Rules Engine, Data Store, Map (MAP-UI), composant 'access', 'batch-report', serveur de réplication MySQL). Value object owned by its system.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Component name as printed, with its short code when one is given (Orchestration (ORC-BS), Login-UI, ingest-external)

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Responsibility of the component as described in the document

attributes.name: layer
attributes.description: Architectural layer or tier the component belongs to when printed (Presentation Layer, Service Layer, Data Access Layer, DFE, DSS, couche métier)

relations.name: kind
relations.description: Kind of component

relations.name: technologies
relations.description: Products, frameworks or standards the component is built on (MongoDB, Elasticsearch, Java, Oracle, IIS)

relations.name: hostedOn
relations.description: The infrastructure nodes the component is deployed on, when the deployment view states it

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: Components are the numbered sub-sections of 'System Architecture', 'System Components', 'Building Block View', 'Logical View', 'Element Catalog', 'Architecture applicative', 'Architecture détaillée' and the boxes of layer and deployment diagrams. One value object per component of the document's main system; sub-components (Drivers, Pipelines, Data Store under 'DFE Layers') are separate components with the parent named in layer.

classes.name: ApplicationSystem
classes.description: An application or information system of the IT landscape: a business application (MMIS, ACCESS, STARS, SADLS, GovInfo, R-ICMS, Vitam, LocAdoc, Co-op Evaluation System), a platform (ESB, data warehouse, GIS server), a portal or an external partner system the organisation exchanges with (Shibboleth, collection agency system, Medicare Beneficiary Database).

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Full name as printed (State Titling and Registration System, Federal Digital System, Regional Integrated Corridor Management System)

attributes.name: acronym
attributes.description: Acronym or short name printed with the full name or used alone (STARS, FDsys, R-ICMS, MMIS, SSIS, MBDSS)

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Purpose and scope of the system as described ('System Overview', 'Purpose of GovInfo', 'Positionnement', 'Enjeux')

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Version or release of the system the document describes (Release 1C.2, 9.1.0, NextGen)

attributes.name: userCount
attributes.description: Number of users when printed

attributes.name: annualCost
attributes.description: Annual cost or budget in the document's currency when printed ($70 million annually)

relations.name: kind
relations.description: Kind of system

relations.name: status
relations.description: Lifecycle status stated or implied by the document (legacy, in production, planned, to be replaced)

relations.name: hosting
relations.description: Hosting model when stated (on premise, SaaS, public cloud, mainframe)

relations.name: owner
relations.description: The organisation that owns or operates the system ('maintained by DIT-T', 'Prepared by GovInfo Program', 'DSI')

relations.name: vendor
relations.description: The vendor, integrator or contractor that built or supplies the system (Gainwell, DXC, Kapsch, Net-Assembly)

relations.name: hostedAt
relations.description: The site or provider data center hosting the system, when stated

relations.name: capabilities
relations.description: Business capabilities or processes the system supports ('supports all Driver and Vehicle services', MITA process-to-system mapping)

relations.name: technologies
relations.description: Products, platforms and standards the system as a whole is built on (mainframe, .NET, PHP, MySQL, OAIS)

relations.name: masterOf
relations.description: Data objects the system is the system of record for ('Records and monitors license plates', 'stores system information')

relations.name: components
relations.description: The subsystems, modules, services and data stores described for the system

relations.name: qualityRequirements
relations.description: Quality attribute requirements and constraints stated for the system

relations.name: decisions
relations.description: Design decisions and orientations recorded for the system

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: The main system is named in the title ('System Design Document for R-ICMS', 'VITAM - Architecture', 'System Architecture Description of LocAdoc') and in 'System Overview', 'Identification', 'Vue d'ensemble'. Other systems appear in 'System Context', 'External Interfaces', 'Interfaces externes du système', 'Significant Systems' lists ('State Automated Driver License System (SADLS) Issues Driver License Credentials'), 'Reference Documents', application maps ('cartographie applicative') and as the source or destination of interfaces. Use the full name as name and the short form in acronym; when only the acronym is printed, use it as the name. Extract external partner systems too, but not products (those are Technology) or organisations.

classes.name: DataElement
classes.description: One field of a file layout or message of an exchange, as printed in interface control documents: field name, position, length, type, whether required, description. Value object owned by its exchange.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Field name as printed in the layout table ('Field Name', 'Data Element', 'Nom du champ')

attributes.name: position
attributes.description: Start position in a fixed-width record when printed ('Position', 'Start')

attributes.name: length
attributes.description: Field length when printed ('Length', 'Size')

attributes.name: dataType
attributes.description: Type or format as printed (X(9), 9(5), Alphanumeric, Date CCYYMMDD, VARCHAR)

attributes.name: required
attributes.description: True when the field is marked required or mandatory ('R', 'Req', 'Obligatoire')

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Meaning and allowed values of the field as printed

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: One value object per row of the 'Field Descriptions', 'Record Layout', 'Header Record' / 'Detail Record' / 'Trailer Record' and 'Data Definitions' tables. Attach the row to the exchange whose file or message the table describes (the table title names it: 'Placement Outbound File Field Descriptions').

classes.name: DataExchange
classes.description: An interface or data flow between two systems: a file transfer over SFTP, a web service or REST API call, a message queue, an EDI transaction, a database extract, a batch feed. Described in interface control documents (ICD), interface specifications, 'System Interfaces' sections and 'flux' sections of French technical architecture documents.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Name of the interface, file or flow as printed (Placement Outbound File, Territory Beneficiary Query, SSIS/MMIS Eligibility Interface, flux d'ingest)

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Purpose of the exchange and the business rules that govern it

attributes.name: protocol
attributes.description: Transport protocol or channel as printed (SFTP, HTTPS/TLS, SOAP, MQ, VPN tunnel, Connect:Direct)

attributes.name: format
attributes.description: Message or file format as printed (fixed-width, CSV, XML, JSON, X12 834, NCPDP D.0, SEDA)

attributes.name: frequency
attributes.description: Frequency or timing as printed (daily, nightly, real-time, weekly on Monday, quotidien)

attributes.name: volume
attributes.description: Volume or size limit as printed ('up to 10k records', '2 Go/jour')

attributes.name: bidirectional
attributes.description: True when the same interface carries data both ways; otherwise source and target give the direction

relations.name: mechanism
relations.description: Integration mechanism used

relations.name: source
relations.description: The system that sends the data ('Source', 'Outbound from', 'émetteur')

relations.name: target
relations.description: The system that receives the data ('Destination', 'Inbound to', 'destinataire')

relations.name: dataObjects
relations.description: The business data objects carried by the exchange

relations.name: dataElements
relations.description: The fields of the file or message layout, when the document prints them

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: Exchanges appear in 'System Interfaces', 'Process/Data Flows', 'Data Exchanges' tables (Table 6), 'Web Service Interfaces', 'File Transfer Interfaces', 'Interfaces externes', 'Flux métier' / 'Flux exploitation' / 'Flux techniques' tables (with columns source, destination, protocole, port, fréquence, volumétrie), and in text ('Approximately 50 federal, state, and local applications connect to DMV systems'). One entity per named file, service or flow; when a document lists an interface between two systems without a name, name it '<source> to <target>'. Point source and target at ApplicationSystem entities, creating the partner system when needed.

classes.name: Project
classes.description: A project, programme or planned initiative that changes the landscape: a modernisation programme (DMV Application System Modernization, NC MAX), a replacement (ERP replacement, 'remplacement du logiciel de gestion administrative'), an infrastructure renewal, a target-state initiative of an EA plan or master plan (schéma directeur).

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Name of the project or programme as printed (DMV Application System Modernization (DASM), Renouvellement des infrastructures serveurs)

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Objective and scope of the project as described

attributes.name: startDate
attributes.description: Start date or year when printed

attributes.name: endDate
attributes.description: Planned or actual end date or year when printed (2025 for a 2021-2025 plan)

attributes.name: budget
attributes.description: Budget or cost in the document's currency when printed ($42 million)

relations.name: status
relations.description: Status stated or implied by the document

relations.name: sponsor
relations.description: The organisation sponsoring or running the project

relations.name: affectedSystems
relations.description: Systems the project replaces, upgrades, migrates or introduces

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: Projects appear in 'Future Plans', 'Future State', 'Transition Plan', 'Roadmap', 'Projets', 'Orientations 2021-2025', audit findings ('46 projects ... $42 million') and modernisation sections. Extract named projects and programmes, not generic recommendations.

classes.name: DocumentRevision
classes.description: One row of a document's revision history: version, date, author and description of the change. Value object owned by its document.

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Version label as printed (1.0, 2.01, v1.2, 0.8, 225-15.3)

attributes.name: date
attributes.description: Date of the revision

attributes.name: author
attributes.description: Author or organisation of the revision as printed in the 'Author' column

attributes.name: changes
attributes.description: Description of the change as printed ('Updated Network Diagram', 'Initial draft', 'Revision based on the comments of ...')

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: One value object per row of the 'Revision History', 'Document History', 'Change Sheet', 'Publication Version Control' or 'Historique des versions' table, usually on the first pages after the cover.

classes.name: ArchitectureDocument
classes.description: The architecture document itself: an enterprise architecture blueprint, a technical architecture document (dossier d'architecture technique, DAT), a system design document (SDD), a software architecture document (SAD), an interface control document (ICD), an IT master plan (schéma directeur du SI, SDSI), a self-assessment or an audit report. Its revisions are value objects.

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Title as printed on the cover, without the version ('System Design Document for R-ICMS', 'VITAM - Architecture', 'Schéma directeur du système d'information')

attributes.name: reference
attributes.description: Document number or identifier when printed (MMA.DDX.1502.04.5.1211, W103, Deliverable 2.1, EA225)

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Version of this edition as printed on the cover ('Version 1.0', 'v7', '9.1.0', 'Revision February / 2026')

attributes.name: publicationDate
attributes.description: Date printed on the cover or approval line ('Approval date: 10/30/2018', 'juin 05, 2026', 'July 2023')

attributes.name: purpose
attributes.description: The 'Purpose', 'Objectif de ce document' or 'Executive Summary' paragraph

attributes.name: pageCount
attributes.description: Number of pages when the document states it ('Page 1 of 38')

attributes.name: confidentiality
attributes.description: Classification or licence printed on the document ('Confidential and Proprietary', 'strictly confidential', 'CC BY 4.0', 'Public')

relations.name: documentType
relations.description: Kind of architecture document

relations.name: language
relations.description: Language the document is written in

relations.name: issuer
relations.description: The organisation that issues the document ('Prepared by', 'Published by', 'Edition :')

relations.name: authors
relations.description: People named as authors, editors or contributors

relations.name: approvers
relations.description: People named as reviewers or approvers in the document control or approval table

relations.name: describedSystems
relations.description: The system or systems the document is about (its main subject, not every system it mentions)

relations.name: revisions
relations.description: The rows of the revision history

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: Exactly one entity per PDF: the document being read. Title, version, date, issuer and reference are on the cover page and in the page header or footer; the revision history is on the pages that follow. Keep the version out of the title so that successive editions of the same document merge (System Design Document v5 and v7 are one document with two revisions). Documents referenced in 'Reference Documents' or 'Documents de référence' are NOT extracted as ArchitectureDocument.

classes.name: ArchitecturePrinciple
classes.description: A guiding principle, guideline or standard rule the organisation applies to its architecture: 'Simpler is better', 'Commercial products should be used where possible', 'Industry based standards should be used', 'Open Source', 'API REST', an EA standard requirement agencies must comply with.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Short name or first words of the principle as printed

attributes.name: statement
attributes.description: The principle and its rationale as written in the document

relations.name: sourceDocument
relations.description: The document that states the principle

stereotypePropertyInstances.valueAsString: Principles are bullet lists under 'Guidelines', 'Guiding Principles', 'Goals', 'Principes d'architecture', 'Orientations générales' or 'Architecture Principles' in EA blueprints, standards and technical architecture documents. One entity per principle; skip generic prose.

enumerations.name: OrganisationKind
enumerations.description: Role an organisation plays in the architecture documents

values.description: A federal, state or local public body (agency, department, ministère, collectivité)
The IT department or directorate of an organisation (OIT, DIT-T, DSI, Programs Strategy and Technology)
A business division, office or programme inside an organisation (Division of Motor Vehicles, GovInfo Program, pôle)
A software or hardware vendor, integrator or contractor (Kapsch, SwRI, Gainwell, DXC, Net-Assembly)
A hosting or cloud provider (Digital Ocean, AWS, Azure)
A standards organisation (NIST, W3C, The Open Group, CMS as a rule maker)
A research or industry consortium (ITEA 2 CREATE consortium)
A university or school (RIT, université)
Any other kind of organisation

enumerations.name: TechnologyCategory
enumerations.description: Category of a technology product, protocol or standard

values.description: Windows Server, Solaris, Linux, Ubuntu, iOS
Oracle, MySQL, SQL Server, MongoDB, SQLite, DynamoDB
Application server, ESB, message broker, search engine, web server (WebSphere, IIS, Elasticsearch, Kafka)
Programming language or framework (Java, J2EE, .NET, PHP, Android)
Hypervisor or container platform (VMware vSphere, Docker, Kubernetes)
Switch, router, wireless, load balancer, VPN (Cisco Nexus, Aruba, Global Protect)
